newsitem.title: USA: Helms urges consultation on China's WTO entry.
newsitem.headline: Helms urges consultation on China's WTO entry.

text.p: Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms Tuesday criticized China's trade policies and urged the administration to consult Congress on China's bid to join the World Trade Organization.

In a letter to Secretary of State Warren Christopher, who is currently in Beijing to talk with senior Chinese officials, Helms said Beijing's threat to retaliate against U.S. actions in a textile dispute raised questions about China's entry into the WTO.
"If China cannot abide by a mere bilateral agreement on textiles, how can the U.S. rely upon China's abiding by the multilateral rules of the WTO?" Helms wrote.
He urged the administration to consult Congress before making a decision on China's WTO bid. "An impasse with Congress can thereby be avoided," Helms said.
In September, the U.S. Trade Representative's office announced it was taking an enforcement action against China for transshipments of textiles in violation of an agreement.
Beijing announced last week that it planned to suspend temporarily imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks in retaliation.
